needs_human.note: A file carrying two case variants of one tag in the source drive (`Alpha` and `alpha`, which uq_tags_drive_name allows) silently ends up with a single tag at the destination, and the spelling kept depends on iteration order when the destination has no row.; retarget_file_tags sweeps every unattached Tag row in the source drive, not only those this file left, so unrelated orphans are deleted in the same move transaction.; If the destination holds both `Alpha` and `alpha`, .first() has no ORDER BY, so which row is reused is not defined.; A destination row's spelling wins over the moved file's. For a Markdown file the frontmatter keeps its own spelling while File.tags shows the destination's, until something re-projects it.

Moving a file merges case variants of a tag on that file into one tag on the destination (`tagops.py:50-51`), which is a visible change only if a file holds both spellings.; A `.md` file moved onto a destination row with a different spelling keeps the row's spelling in `File.tags` while its frontmatter keeps its own. A later `replace_file_tags` from the frontmatter renames the destination row for every file on that drive (`backend/app/routers/files.py:169-172`), so the row's spelling is only preserved until then.; Each cross-drive move also sweeps every other orphan tag row on the source drive, not only rows this file left (`tagops.py:59`).; A non-ASCII tag differing only in case between drives, such as `Übung` and `übung`, does not match and produces two rows on the destination, because of the same folding mismatch as F1.
